newsitem.title: USA: Big ad agencies report good year, expect slowdown.
newsitem.headline: Big ad agencies report good year, expect slowdown.

text.p: Advertising agencies are basking in a period of high growth amid two years of record media spending by brand managers, but the boom is expected to moderate in 1997, agency chiefs said at an industry conference.
The past two years have marked a time of "exceptional above-trend performance," said Fred J. Meyer, chief financial officer of Omnicom Group Inc at the PaineWebber Media Conference.
Meyer said double-digit growth will continue at Omnicom's foreign operations but "gradual moderation in the domestic market's growth" will temper the company's overall performance.
So far this year, revenue at Omnicom, parent of the BBDO and DDB Needham agencies, has climbed 18 percent, while profit per share is up 22 percent.
Results for the full year expected to show similar gains. For the year, net profit will reach $2.20 a share, up from $1.89 in 1995, Omnicom President John Wren said.

Omnicom's rival, Interpublic Group of Cos Inc, has enjoyed robust growth, too. Its chairman, Philip Geier, concurred with estimates that his group, the largest media advertising company in the world, will show a gain in earnings of about 14 percent to $2.45 a share.

The two major advertising groups both reported adding about $1.0 billion in new business this year. Still, the biggest agencies are concerned over an increase in churning of secondary accounts and see growth in new business tapering off.

"What we're finding is that package goods brands are now consolidating into the top one, two and three positions in each category," Geier said. Advertising support is being phased out for some secondary brands.

The churn in new accounts can prove costly for agencies, as they lose a revenue stream during the period of consolidation. Cordiant Plc Chairman Robert Seelert said that his agencies, Saatchi & Saatchi and Bates Worldwide, were winning accounts but finding their operating profits under pressure.

The British agency companies, Cordiant and WPP Plc, owner of Ogilvy & Mather, trail the leading American groups in financial performance, largely because of costly acquisitions in the past decade. But officials of both told the conference that their financial houses are in order and they are in position to show solid gains.
Robert Lerwill, WPP's chief financial officer, said: "We are working towards more improvement. We are not as profitable as Omnicom and IPG (Interpublic), but we are getting there."

Lerwill said the company had substantially paid down its huge debt -- mostly accrued in the acquisitions of Ogilvy and Mather and J Walter Thompson in the 1980s. He said WPP's share price reflected the company's firmer financial footing by outperforming the industry substantially over the past year.
"We're not just focused on repaying debt anymore. We are focusing on maximizing shareholder value," he said.
